title: Penne con Tonno e Olive
subtitle: Tinned tuna, black olives, and tomato
excerpt: A quick storecupboard pasta of tinned tuna, black olives, capers, and tomato. The whole thing comes together in the time it takes to boil the pasta.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pasta with tuna and olives is a standard Italian pantry pasta found across the country. The version here follows the southern Italian approach: olive oil, tomato, tuna in oil, olives, and capers. It requires no fresh ingredients and makes a complete meal from the storecupboard.

content.text: Penne con tonno e olive is the pasta you make when the fridge is empty. Everything comes from tins and jars: tuna in olive oil, black olives, capers, tinned tomatoes. The tuna goes in last so it stays in large flakes rather than breaking up into dry crumbs. Tuna in oil is essential, tuna in brine gives a flat, dry result.

Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the garlic (and chilli if using) and cook gently for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes, crushing them with a spoon, along with the olives, capers, and oregano. Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce reduces slightly.
Cook the penne in well-salted boiling water. Reserve a cup of pasta water before draining.

Add the drained penne to the sauce and toss. Add the tuna in large chunks and stir gently, you want it to break into flakes, not mush. Add a splash of pasta water if needed. Season with black pepper and scatter over the parsley. No cheese.
